The Big Story · Weather

The storm is violent. The forecast is not a Japan landfall.

Typhoon Koguma carried 65-meter-per-second gusts east of Japan this morning. The same official forecast turns it north over open water. Understanding both facts is the difference between useful caution and panic.

Japan’s postseason can end a series before Game 3.

Both Central and Pacific League Climax Series first-stage matchups continue at 2 p.m. JST. The higher regular-season seed advances with two wins—and also advances if the best-of-three ends tied, giving “home advantage” a literal postseason rule.

Japanese word of the day進路 · shinro

Shinro means a course, route or path ahead. 進 means “advance” and 路 means “road.” It can describe a student’s future after school, but weather reports use taifū no shinro for a typhoon’s projected path. Example: Taifū no shinro wa kawaru kanōsei ga arimasu—“The typhoon’s track may change.” Today’s forecast is a shinro, not a rail fixed to the ocean.
